quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, open doors, or stick arms out windows. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: When a car passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on the left. Riding on the right side may encourage the other driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group ride?

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch over less experienced riders.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to improve your view.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after finishing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about where you are going.

questions.question: What does the "SEE" strategy stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When can a motorized bicycle or moped use a bicycle lane?

options.text: Never. Motorized bicycles may never be used in bicycle lanes.
Only when carrying a passenger.
Only when authorized by local ordinance or law enforcement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when authorized by local ordinance or law enforcement.
questions.explanation: Motorized bicycles and mopeds can use bicycle lanes only if local laws or law enforcement allow it.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
A windshield protects you from the wind, but goggles won't.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield won't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position that allows you to most effectively see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle to see clearly and be seen by others. For a left curve, ride on the right side to spot oncoming traffic early. For a right curve, ride in the left-center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly. Keep your motorcycle straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down and leave the road once your speed is low enough.

questions.question: How do convex mirrors differ from regular mirrors?

options.text: They provide a more narrow view of the road.
They provide a wider view of the road.
They provide a better view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make vehicles look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: The front and rear brakes need to be used at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to increase stability of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn. It can cause the bike to tip. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the U-turn.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, you may continue through.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, position your motorcycle at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb. One wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: For motorcycle operators, eye protection is:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators must wear proper eye protection when riding.

questions.question: If you will be carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely have to:

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure adjustments.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to increase tire pressure a few pounds. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure to use.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride wherever you are most comfortable.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding on the left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This helps you avoid doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to change your position if conditions change.

questions.question: When attempting to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the speed limit. Pass only when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard on the road, you should NOT:

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Always communicate with other drivers. Use your horn, lights, and signals to let them know you are there. Slow down to a safe speed and change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: When wearing a protective jacket while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.
Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: A sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being tightened properly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: Front wheel wobbling is usually caused by improper weight loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider should NOT place a toll road transponder:

options.text: On the windshield.
In their pocket.
Under the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under the seat.
questions.explanation: Transponders can be placed in your pocket, in a cycle net on the gas tank, on a license plate device, in a storage compartment, or on the windshield. The toll reader must be able to detect it.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Approach intersections with caution. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of your lane that makes other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane that makes other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in your lane so other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders may cause you to steer incorrectly.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road means:

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far part of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is a good idea because you will be farther away.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far part of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not a good idea because you will not get used to any part of the lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other drivers.
A smart choice when adjusting to changing road or traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A smart choice when adjusting to changing road or traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.
